problem: Prior data-driven image-goal navigation methods use simple network architectures trained from scratch, which limits performance in challenging situations such as multiple turns or varying lighting.
motivation: Image-goal navigation requires a robot to reach a location specified by an image, and robust performance in unseen and challenging environments is needed for real deployment. The authors analyze which features are essential for visual navigation and argue that pretrained foundation-model features plus better goal encoding can improve this.
key_idea: Use a pretrained foundation model for visual feature extraction, encode the goal image with cross attention, and apply a token attention mechanism that dynamically weights tokens for image-goal navigation.
insight: From the abstract only: pretrained foundation features combined with cross-attention goal encoding and token weighting yield stronger generalization to unseen environments and to challenging conditions than from-scratch simple networks. No ablation details are available in the provided text.
method: Foundation-model feature extractor: a pretrained visual foundation model replaces a from-scratch encoder to extract observation features.
Cross-attention goal encoding: the goal image is fused with the observations via cross attention.
Token attention mechanism: dynamically assigns weights to different tokens before the policy output.

setting.backbone: Pretrained visual foundation model (unspecified in abstract) with cross-attention and token-attention layers
setting.observation: RGB images (current observation and goal image)
